Patients who previously received radiotherapy for primary rectal cancer treatment have worse oncologic outcomes than those who had not received radiotherapy after pelvic exenteration for locally recurrent rectal cancer. This is because prior radiation therapy can lead to changes in the tumor biology, making it more resistant to further treatments.

In other words, patients who underwent radiotherapy before undergoing pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer may have a worse prognosis compared to those who received no prior treatment or only received neoadjuvant chemoradiation.
